subject: Announce: Package to assist in TMB debugging

messages.author: 8c7e386b9728df46
messages.subject: Announce: Package to assist in TMB debugging
parts:
BuildSys is an R package that aids in debugging C/C++ dynamic libraries built for interfacing with R. It makes building dynamic libraries in R simple but transparent (rather than the more opaque approach that R provides). It does so by providing an S4 class that represents and creates a permanent (rather than transient) GNU makefile and using GNU make to build the library. When libraries build correctly this is inconsequential but when there are build issues this is where having access to the raw makefile becomes important in debugging the build process.

The more important part of the package that would most interest you is that it provides an easy mechanism to debug C/C++ code within the dynamic library through the use of the gdb-MI / lldb-MI interface support available in Microsoft Visual Code (a freely available code editor supported on Windows, Linux and MacOS). With this mechanism you will be able to easily debug you TMB code through the hosting and control of gdb/lldb through the easy to use GUI interface that Microsoft Visual Code (as opposed to the more complex command line approach of native gdb / lldb) provides.

If this interests you then you can find the package here:

https://github.com/pjumppanen/BuildSys/releases/tag/1.0.4

A note to MacOS users, on my testing machine I could not install the package from the .tar.gz file. If this occurs you can resolve this by deleting the partial.rdb file in the folder BuildSys_1.0.4.tar/BuildSys/build/ in the .tar.gz archive.

Once installed you can find out how to use it by running,

require(BuildSys)
?BuildSys

in R. Please consult the "Software Installation Requirements for Debugging" section in the above help before attempting to debug. A note of warning to Windows users is that although Microsoft Visual Code theoretically supports debugging of 32 bit gcc compiled code, the debugging functionality does not currently work so please use a 64 bit version of R.

A simple example illustrating the workflow with this package would be (assuming R or Rstudio is open in a folder with a single .cpp source file containing you TMB code),

# load required packages
require(TMB)
require(BuildSys)

# create build project
Project <- new("BSysProject")

# make / compile the code to build a debuggable dynamic lib
Project <- make(Project)

# load the library into R
loadLibrary(Project)

# do whatever common R setup code you need to do
# to run you TMB code. That is, everything up to but
# not including the call to MakeADFun()
.
.
.

# open a debug session in Microsoft Visual Code
vcDebug(Project)


At this point on calling vcDebug() Microsoft Visual Code will open and you can set breakpoints in your C++ code within the editor. Now select the "Run/Start Debugging..." menu in Visual Code and on doing so a new R session will be launched that will have the same state as the parent R/Rstudio session at the point vcDebug() was called. In this new R session simply run whatever commands (less the initialisation stuff you already did in the parent session) you need to to debug the code. When it gets called and the breakpoints get hit, execution will drop out into Microsoft Visual Code, at which point you will be able to see the contents of variables, single step through the code and the like.

regards,


Paavo Jumppanen.
